name: rain-b7e7b820-blind30-ots
instr:
# rain — a peer-to-peer transfer client giving wrong answers from the remote interface down to the wire, without a test suite

I have been putting a build from the current tree through its paces and it gives wrong answers in an alarming number of unrelated places. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the wire format changed and nothing about my own scripts changed; the same operations that used to work now come back wrong, and in several places an operation that used to succeed is refused outright. Everything below is something I reproduced by hand, in roughly the order I hit it.

Driving the daemon through its remote-control interface is broken from the very first call. On a freshly started daemon with nothing registered at all, asking for the list of active transfers comes back with one entry in it instead of an empty list, and that same phantom entry inflates the reported count after a real transfer is there. Handing the daemon a metadata file to take on reports an error back to the caller even though the work goes through and an id and info hash are produced for it. Asking for the statistics of a transfer that has no failure recorded against it makes the call fail outright instead of returning a statistics record. Asking for the magnet link of a transfer the daemon is already holding returns an error rather than text beginning with magnet:?xt=urn:btih:.
